221: D is correct because Amazon S3 provides durable, low-cost object storage that is ideal for a 7-year retention requirement, and it can be combined with lifecycle policies for cost control. S3 also lets the reporting tool access any or all log files concurrently over HTTP, which is far more cost-effective than block or file storage tied to individual instances at this scale.
222: A is correct because cross-account IAM role delegation is the AWS-recommended way to grant access to a third party that has its own AWS account. The company creates a role in its account whose trust policy allows the vendor's IAM role to assume it, and attaches policies granting only the permissions the vendor's tool needs. The vendor's automated tool then uses sts:AssumeRole to obtain temporary credentials, avoiding long-term credentials or IAM users.
223: A is correct because attaching an IAM role with sufficient privileges to the EKS pod (using IAM roles for service accounts) gives the application temporary, automatically rotated credentials to call DynamoDB without hardcoded keys. D is correct because a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB is a gateway endpoint that lets the application in private subnets reach DynamoDB over the AWS private network, so no traffic traverses the internet. Together these steps provide both authorized credential-free access and a fully private network path.
224: C is correct because a Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy returns multiple healthy records for the domain and clients randomly select among them, distributing traffic across all running instances while automatically removing unhealthy endpoints. E is correct because launching four instances evenly split across two Availability Zones provides high availability and fault tolerance, since losing an instance or an entire AZ still leaves running capacity in the other AZ. An uneven two-plus-one split would not provide balanced fault tolerance.
225: B is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, serverless ingestion service that automatically scales and can deliver streaming data directly to Amazon Redshift. Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale data warehouse that supports standard SQL, enabling on-demand analytics of both existing and newly arriving data. This serverless pipeline minimizes operational overhead because no ingestion infrastructure must be provisioned or managed.
226: E is correct because using Amazon API Gateway with a Kinesis data stream and Kinesis Data Firehose replaces the single EC2 ingestion instance with a fully managed, serverless pipeline that can absorb data from millions of devices and reliably deliver it to Amazon S3. A is correct because AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service that can process and transform the raw data after it lands in S3, eliminating the need to run transformation logic on managed EC2 instances. Together these steps decouple ingestion from processing so each scales independently with minimal operational overhead.
227: B is correct because S3 Versioning retains every prior version of each object, and the existing lifecycle rule only deletes current versions, so old noncurrent versions keep accumulating and the object count rises. Configuring the lifecycle policy to also expire noncurrent versions deletes objects older than 3 years using a native, fully automated S3 feature at no extra cost. This is simpler and cheaper than writing custom code and cannot be accomplished through CloudTrail or object ownership settings.
228: C is correct because writing incoming data to an Amazon SQS queue decouples the API from the database, and the durable queue buffers messages during traffic spikes so no data is lost. An AWS Lambda function invoked by SQS then drains the queue and writes to the RDS instance at a controlled rate with a bounded number of connections. This smooths out the write load and eliminates the timeout errors caused by the database being overwhelmed.
229: A is correct because Aurora Serverless for MySQL is MySQL-compatible, so the existing databases migrate naturally, and it automatically and instantly scales compute capacity up or down based on demand. Aurora also delivers improved performance, storage that grows automatically, and six copies of data replicated across three Availability Zones for durability, all with minimal operational effort. This removes the manual replication and scaling work currently done on EC2.
230: C is correct because NAT gateways are a fully managed service that automatically scales up to 100 Gbps of bandwidth and is highly available within its Availability Zone with no management effort. Deploying one NAT gateway in each of two different Availability Zones removes the single point of failure, because outbound connectivity survives the loss of an entire AZ, which two gateways in the same AZ would not.
231: B is correct because a VPC peering connection is a private network link between the two VPCs that routes traffic over private IP addresses inside the AWS network, keeping the database inaccessible from the internet. The database security group can then allow traffic only from the application's subnet or security group, providing secure, controlled access rather than exposure via public IP addresses.
232: C is correct because VPC flow logs capture metadata about every network connection, including accepted RDP and SSH sessions, and publishing them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs enables metric filters that detect that traffic. A CloudWatch metric alarm on those filters can trigger a notification so the operations team is alerted whenever RDP or SSH access to an environment is established. This works across all the isolated VPCs and detects actual established connections rather than only instance state changes.
233: A is correct because using a strong password on the root user is a fundamental step in protecting it against brute-force and dictionary attacks. B is correct because enabling multi-factor authentication on the root user is the single most important safeguard, protecting the account even if the password is compromised. Both actions follow AWS best practices of securing root and then avoiding its daily use.
234: C is correct because AWS KMS keys are the correct mechanism for encrypting data at rest, supporting both EBS volume encryption and Aurora database storage encryption. An ACM certificate attached to the Application Load Balancer is the correct way to encrypt data in transit, providing TLS termination for client connections to the application. These managed services together encrypt all application data at rest and in transit with minimal configuration.
235: C is correct because migrating from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration, so the AWS Schema Conversion Tool is required to convert the Oracle schema and database code to PostgreSQL before the data moves. AWS DMS with a full load plus change data capture (CDC) task performs the initial copy and then continuously replicates ongoing changes, keeping both databases in sync while applications are migrated one by one over several months. A memory-optimized replication instance provides the capacity to handle the high volume of reads and writes during continuous replication.
236: D is correct because load-balanced Multi-AZ Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end and application layers add scalability and high availability while preserving the existing EC2-based architecture, requiring the least amount of change to the application. Moving the MySQL database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance provides automated failover and durability for the data tier. Storing and serving user images from Amazon S3 offloads the heaviest traffic to a scalable and durable object store.
237: A is correct because VPC peering works across separate AWS accounts and provides a private, direct network connection between VPC-A and VPC-B using private IP addresses. A peering connection is a logical routing configuration rather than a single device, so it has no single point of failure and no bandwidth bottleneck. Gateway endpoints would not work here because they only reach AWS public services such as S3 or DynamoDB, not EC2 instances.
238: C is correct because AWS Budgets is the purpose-built, low-cost service for tracking spend and sending alerts when thresholds are exceeded. Creating a monthly cost budget scoped to EC2 instances for each account, with an alert threshold and an SNS topic for notification, tells the company as soon as EC2 usage in an account exceeds the threshold. This requires no servers or custom analytics pipelines, making it the most cost-effective option.
239: A is correct because an Amazon API Gateway REST API provides a managed HTTPS endpoint out of the box and integrates directly with the Go Lambda function, letting clients reach the microservice with standard HTTPS calls. Enabling IAM authentication on the API makes API Gateway verify IAM-signed requests, so the Lambda function requires no custom authentication logic. This fully managed front door is the most operationally efficient way to expose an IAM-authenticated HTTPS endpoint for the microservice.
240: D is correct because hosting the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse means the large 50 MB query result sets never leave the Region, incurring no data transfer egress charges. Only the small 500 KB web pages are transferred out, over the Direct Connect connection, keeping egress volume minimal. Hosting the tool on premises would force every 50 MB result set across the Direct Connect or internet path, dramatically increasing data transfer costs.
